In [[mathematics]], an [[Group action (mathematics)|action]] of a [[group (mathematics)|group]] ''G'' on a [[topological space]] ''X'' is '''cocompact''' if the [[Quotient space (topology)|quotient space]] ''X''/''G'' is a [[compact space]]. If ''X'' is [[locally compact]], then an equivalent condition is that there is a compact subset ''K'' of ''X'' such that the image of ''K'' under the action of ''G'' covers ''X''.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://mathoverflow.net/questions/110407 |title=Characterization of cocompact group actione |publisher=MathOverflow |access-date=2026-04-25}}</ref>  It is sometimes referred to as ''mpact'', a tongue-in-cheek reference to [[Duality (mathematics)|dual]] notions where prefixing with "co-" twice would "cancel out".
